headline: Orlando's fandom runs on a tourist-calendar clock: a loud April-May playoff peak, a long Cup-and-holiday winter shoulder, and a hurricane-season-to-Halloween autumn where the Magic compete with Universal, Disney and college football for attention.
summary: The Magic are a young-core, second-wave-hype team (Banchero, Wagner, Bane, plus returning center Vucevic) coming off a 45-37 season, a Play-In win over Charlotte and a first-round loss to Detroit, now under new coach Sean Sweeney. Fan intensity is playoff-gated: it spikes in April and May and sags in the dead heat of summer, when tourism, theme-park seasonal events and the Orlando Summer League are the only hoops touchpoints. Unlike coastal markets, a large share of the arena and the retail audience is visitors, so game-night and gift purchases follow the tourism calendar as much as the standings. The Magic have no opening-night or Christmas Day game this year, so the first real spike is the Cup Friday run in Nov, the holiday gifting window, and a playoff push that depends on a healthy Franz Wagner.

insights.title: Playoff-gated peak, summer trough
insights.detail: Engagement is highest in April-May when the Magic are in the postseason and lowest in July-September, when the only team touchpoints are the Orlando Summer League and draft aftermath amid peak heat and hurricane season. Last season's 8-seed run and first-round exit with a Play-In win over Charlotte kept the spring peak short.
insights.implication: Hold the biggest apparel drop for a playoff-ready window (mid-March to April) and keep summer product to lifestyle and heritage, not performance jerseys.

insights.title: The visitor multiplier
insights.detail: Orlando's tourism economy means Kia Center nights in Dec, Mar and the summer school breaks carry a large share of out-of-market buyers who treat the Magic as a souvenir, not a loyalty badge. Visitors buy in the arena and at Disney Springs-area retail rather than online.
insights.implication: Build a small giftable, travel-friendly capsule (tees, caps, packable items) priced for visitors, separate from the locals' jersey-and-City-Edition stack.

insights.title: Black Friday-to-Christmas is a Cup-anchored winter
insights.detail: Magic are in Emirates NBA Cup East Group A with Detroit, Toronto, Milwaukee and Brooklyn, with group games on Fridays from Oct 30 to Nov 27. The Magic have no opening-night or Christmas Day game, so holiday hoops attention goes elsewhere.
insights.implication: Use Cup Friday nights as the local activation beat and the Cup colorway or tee as the gift item, rather than leaning on national-TV moments the Magic do not have.

insights.title: Football and Florida fall compete directly
insights.detail: From September to December, UCF Knights, Florida, Florida State and Miami football, plus the Florida Classic in Orlando in November, dominate local sports attention. Orlando City SC and the Orlando Pride share the same fall calendar.
insights.implication: Do not launch performance basketball product in October; use collegiate-adjacent crossover looks and lean on the Magic's pinstripe heritage to stand out from football.

insights.title: Heritage nostalgia is a second engine
insights.detail: The 1995 Finals team (Shaquille O'Neal, Penny Hardaway, Nick Anderson), the 2009 Dwight Howard Finals team and the pinstripe era of jerseys still anchor local identity among fans who grew up in the 90s. This sentiment peaks around the draft, 'Throwback' nights and opening weeks.
insights.implication: Pair every Banchero-era release with a Penny-era pinstripe or star motif story so older and younger fans both have a reason to buy.

insights.title: Hurricane season sets a quiet clock
insights.detail: Atlantic hurricane season runs June to November, and a storm week can cancel local events and shift game schedules or shipping. Peak storm risk is Aug-Oct, exactly when preseason hype and early retail would normally build.
insights.implication: Plan a flexible ship window for the Oct-Nov drops and avoid tying a one-night activation to a single early-season date.

designCues.use: Use as the base for Association and gift items so the core read is instantly Orlando.

designCues.source: Franchise secondary silver and the 90s palette
designCues.use: Metallic trim or reflective detail on throwback-inspired pieces.
Statement and night-game pieces; pairs with blue for the modern look.

designCues.source: The 1990s Magic pinstripe uniforms and star motif
designCues.use: Apply to a heritage capsule with clear credit to the Penny-era design; check licensing for any retired marks.
Lightweight, quick-dry knits and mesh for tees and warm-up pieces that work through the long summer.

designCues.cue: Sunset gradient from lake and sky
designCues.source: Central Florida evening skies over downtown lakes
designCues.use: Use as a subtle fade on gift tees and caps, not as a direct theme-park reference.

productHooks: A March-April playoff-push capsule (tee, warm-up, cap) timed to the Play-In window, with a quick-turn playoff-gear plan for rally towels and tees.
A heritage pinstripe capsule built around the 90s Magic, released around the Cup Friday run and holiday gifting.
A visitor-friendly gift line sold at Kia Center and tourist retail: packable tees and caps in Magic blue, priced for souvenirs.
A summer lightweight line timed to Orlando Summer League and school break for fans who engage only at the margins.
watchouts: Avoid any Disney, Universal or theme-park character or logo cues; they are heavily licensed third-party IP.
Pulse remembrance and the LGBTQ+ and Latino communities connected to it must not be used as marketing hooks.
Do not hinge a plan on a Wagner-healthy spring; offer product that works if the team stumbles.
Some schedule details are not yet verified, so confirm home dates before locking activation.
